title: data: clearing an optional unique text field stores an empty string, so the second record whose field is cleared is refused 409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION
body:
domain:devx#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXSZs9PBUc2H8z6mtB

Filing gate: ① product defect with a named landing point and a reproduction (reach: the console record form and `POST`/`PATCH /api/v1/data/OBJECT`, reproduced on two scratch objects).
Business reason: optional unique fields are common: SKU, external code, employee number, tax id. A user who empties that field on one record succeeds. When they empty it on a second record, they get "A record with this value already exists" and cannot save, although both records now have no value. The only workaround is to type a dummy value, which pollutes the data. Imports with blank cells hit the same refusal. records-forms.field-unique-enforcement acceptance[1] asserts that absent values do not collide; a cleared field is the everyday way a value becomes absent.
Reader who acts: the lane that owns the write path (`packages/objectql`, empty-to-null normalisation for an optional text field on write), or the ui form renderer (send `null` on clear). Triage picks the layer; the server side also covers REST and import callers.
Dedupe: `unique cleared field UNIQUE_VIOLATION` 55 hits, all closed and other shapes: #23686, #23714, #23701 (unique refusal wording/locating), #26891 (refusal marks the field), #26867. `unique empty string` 474 (run records). No card covers empty-string collision.

QA-source: #29172 · records-forms.field-unique-enforcement · observed beside the clauses

## What happens

A cleared optional text field is sent and stored as `''`. The tenant-scoped unique index on that field then treats `''` as a real value. The second record cleared, or created with `''`, collides.

Measured at framework `7fa9873f` (main, 2026-11-02) on a stock showcase boot (scratch package), Console built from the same tree.

## Reproduction

1. Create a package with namespace `qauniq`: `POST /api/v1/packages` `{"manifest":{"id":"com.objectstack.qa.unique","name":"QA unique fixture","version":"1.0.0","type":"app","namespace":"qauniq"},"enableOnInstall":true}`.
2. Create an object: `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qauniq_clear?package=com.objectstack.qa.unique` `{"name":"qauniq_clear","label":"QA Unique Clear","sharingModel":"public_read_write","fields":{"name":{"type":"text","label":"Name","required":true},"sku":{"type":"text","label":"SKU","unique":true}}}`.
3. Create two rows: `POST /api/v1/data/qauniq_clear` with `{"name":"r1","sku":"S1"}`, then with `{"name":"r2","sku":"S2"}`.
4. In the console, open r1, choose Edit, clear SKU and click Update. The PATCH body is `{"sku":""}` and the answer is 200. The DB column holds `''`.
5. Do the same on r2. The PATCH `{"sku":""}` answers **409 `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`**, and the modal shows "A record with this value already exists".
6. Over REST the same happens: `POST {"name":"x","sku":""}` twice answers 201, then 409.
7. **Expected:** an emptied optional unique field holds no value, and records with no value do not collide.

## Mechanism (read at 7fa9873f)

- The form sends `''` for a cleared text input. The write path stores `''` verbatim.
- The same `''` lands for `f_lookup` and `f_select` on `showcase_field_zoo`. There, validators already treat `''` as empty: `required` refuses it, and select/lookup skip it.
- The unique index (`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uniq_<object>_organization_id_<field> ON (organization_id, <field>)`, from `uniqueIndexesFromFields` in the SQL driver's `schema-drift.ts`) compares `''` as a value. NULL-distinct semantics therefore never apply to a cleared field.
